hook: The brain of your phone started as sand.
visual_style: Photorealistic cinematic film still, real materials and textures, shallow depth of field, clean-room amber and violet light, mirror-like silicon and brushed steel
world: Chipmaking today: a sunlit quartz sand quarry, then amber-lit clean rooms of a modern chip factory
through_line: silicon, from a handful of sand to a mirror wafer to one chip in a hand

cast.Technician: a technician in a full white clean-room suit, hood, face mask and blue gloves, only the eyes visible

props.Ingot: a long silver-grey cylindrical silicon crystal ingot with a pointed tip
props.Wafer: a round mirror-polished silicon wafer, its surface shimmering with a fine rainbow grid

places.Clean room: a chip factory clean room in amber light, rows of white machines, a smooth grey floor

cta: Comment which piece of tech we should break down next.

captions.hook_line: The chip in your phone started as sand. Here's how it becomes billions of transistors 💻
captions.body: Silicon is purified, melted and grown into a single-crystal ingot, sliced into wafers and polished to a mirror. Circuits are printed with light; the most advanced machines make extreme ultraviolet light by hitting about 50,000 tiny tin droplets a second with lasers. Layer by layer, billions of transistors form, then the wafer is cut into chips.

blocks.narration: The brain of your phone started as sand. Turning that into a chip takes the most precise machines ever built.

blocks.narration: First, silicon is purified and melted down. A seed crystal slowly pulls out one huge, perfect crystal, called an ingot.
blocks.visual: Chunks of grey silicon melting into a glowing orange pool inside a quartz crucib

shots.visual: Chunks of grey silicon melting into a glowing orange pool inside a quartz crucible
The Ingot being slowly drawn upward out of the glowing melt, rotating as it rises
beats: it rises out of the glow

blocks.narration: The ingot is sliced into thin wafers, and each one is polished smoother than almost anything else on Earth.
blocks.visual: A thin wire saw slicing through the Ingot, a stack of thin discs falling away

shots.visual: A thin wire saw slicing through the Ingot, a stack of thin discs falling away
The Wafer spinning on a polishing pad until it turns into a perfect mirror
beats: a reflection sharpens on its surface

blocks.narration: Then light prints the circuits, smaller than a virus. The best machines fire lasers at tiny tin droplets, fifty thousand times a second.
blocks.visual: A violet beam of light shining down through a lens onto the Wafer in the Clean r

shots.visual: A violet beam of light shining down through a lens onto the Wafer in the Clean room
Tiny silver droplets falling through a vacuum chamber, each one flashing bright violet as a laser hits it
A rapid stream of droplets bursting into violet flashes inside the chamber

blocks.narration: Layer after layer, billions of transistors stack up. Then the wafer is cut into chips, and one ends up in your hand.
